report.summary: Claim 8.10 is unfalsifiable: 'never auto-promote them' cannot be observed because 'auto-promote' is undefined and no threshold is given.
risks: 8.10 | high | 'never auto-promote them' is unfalsifiable: the term 'auto-promote' is undefined, and there is no observable threshold or condition that would count as a violation. | Define 'auto-promote' operationally (e.g., any promotion without human approval) and specify the observation (e.g., check promotion log for absence of human signature).

8.11 | medium | 'sealed owner-controlled path' is unfalsifiable: 'sealed' and 'owner-controlled' are not defined, so no observation can confirm or refute the claim. | Define 'sealed' (e.g., requires cryptographic signature from a specific key) and 'owner-controlled' (e.g., only a designated role can initiate). Test by attempting promotion without the key.

8.2 | medium | 'exact source revision' is unfalsifiable: 'exact' is ambiguous (e.g., commit hash? diff? tree state?) and no tolerance is given. | Specify what constitutes an exact revision (e.g., a git commit hash) and test by building from two supposedly identical revisions and verifying the Forest is identical.

8.7 | low | 'revision-aware delta' is unfalsifiable: the term is undefined, so no observation can confirm its presence or correctness. | Define 'revision-aware delta' (e.g., a diff that includes metadata about the source revision) and test by checking that the delta contains that metadata.

8.9 | low | 'signed/traceable receipt' is unfalsifiable: 'signed' and 'traceable' are not defined. | Define the signature scheme and traceability requirements (e.g., receipt includes a hash chain) and test by verifying the signature and trace.

8.4 | low | 'verified project evidence' is unfalsifiable: 'verified' is not defined. | Define the verification process (e.g., must pass automated checks with specific criteria) and test by checking that all evidence in the capsule has been verified.

8.3 | low | 'Select formulation, parent, one operator axis, model, and evaluation fidelity' is unfalsifiable: 'one operator axis' is undefined. | Define 'operator axis' as a specific dimension (e.g., mutation rate) and test by checking that only one such dimension is changed.
8.1 | low | 'controlled loop' is unfalsifiable: 'controlled' is not defined. | Define what controls are in place (e.g., all steps must be logged and reversible) and test by checking logs.

8.12 | low | 'Campaigns factorize evolution' is unfalsifiable: 'factorize' is not defined. | Define 'factorize' as changing exactly one major axis at a time and test by examining the campaign's changes.

8.13 | low | 'Code, prompts, operators, evaluators, and orchestration do not silently co-evolve' is unfalsifiable: 'silently co-evolve' is not defined. | Define 'silently co-evolve' as any unplanned simultaneous change and test by auditing the campaign's changes.
8.6 | low | 'content-addressed storage' is falsifiable but the claim is weak: it is a design choice, not a testable assertion. | Test by storing a candidate and retrieving it by its content hash.
todos: Define 'auto-promote' with an operational threshold (e.g., promotion without explicit human approval) to make claim 8.10 falsifiable.
Define 'sealed owner-controlled path' (e.g., requires a specific cryptographic key) to make claim 8.11 falsifiable.
Define 'exact source revision' (e.g., a specific git commit hash) to make claim 8.2 falsifiable.
Define all undefined terms in claims 8.3, 8.4, 8.7, 8.9, 8.12, 8.13.
Add a note that the loop is intended to be falsifiable and define key terms.

claims.claim: Every campaign follows this controlled loop.
claims.why: The term 'controlled' is undefined. Without a definition of what constitutes a controlled loop, no observation can confirm or refute the claim. To make it falsifiable, define the control mechanisms (e.g., all steps must be logged and reversible) and specify how to observe them.

claims.claim: Build the base Forest for an exact source revision.
claims.why: 'Exact source revision' is ambiguous. It could mean a commit hash, a diff, a tree state, etc. Without a precise definition, one cannot determine whether the Forest was built from an exact revision. To make it falsifiable, specify what counts as an exact revision (e.g., a git commit hash) and test by building from two supposedly identical revisions and verifying the Forest is identical.

claims.claim: Select formulation, parent, one operator axis, model, and evaluation fidelity.
claims.why: 'One operator axis' is undefined. What constitutes an operator axis? Without a definition, one cannot verify that only one axis was selected. To make it falsifiable, define an operator axis as a specific dimension (e.g., mutation rate) and test by checking that only one such dimension is changed in the selection.

claims.claim: Compile a minimal Context Capsule from verified project evidence.
claims.why: 'Verified project evidence' is undefined. What does 'verified' mean? Without a definition, one cannot confirm that the evidence is indeed verified. To make it falsifiable, define the verification process (e.g., evidence must pass automated checks with specific criteria) and test by checking that all evidence in the capsule has been verified.

'Isolated' and 'capability-bounded' are undefined. What constitutes isolation? What bounds? Without definitions, the claim cannot be tested. To make it falsifiable, define isolation (e.g., no network access) and capability bounds (e.g., limited CPU time) and test by monitoring the trial environment.

claims.claim: Store the candidate source tree in content-addressed storage.
claims.why: This claim is a design statement, not an empirical claim. However, it is falsifiable in principle: one could test whether the storage is content-addressed by storing a candidate and retrieving it by its content hash. If retrieval fails, the claim is false. But as a plan requirement, it is more of a specification than a testable hypothesis.

claims.claim: Build a candidate Forest and revision-aware delta.
claims.why: 'Revision-aware delta' is undefined. What makes a delta revision-aware? Without a definition, no observation can confirm its presence. To make it falsifiable, define revision-aware delta as a diff that includes metadata about the source revision (e.g., commit hash) and test by examining the delta for that metadata.

claims.claim: Run the evaluation cascade from cheap validity checks to held-out tests.
claims.why: 'Cheap validity checks' and 'held-out tests' are undefined. What counts as cheap? What are held-out tests? Without definitions, one cannot verify the cascade. To make it falsifiable, define the specific checks and tests (e.g., unit tests for cheap, cross-validation for held-out) and test by inspecting the evaluation pipeline.

claims.claim: Emit a signed/traceable receipt and archive all outcomes.
claims.why: 'Signed/traceable receipt' is undefined. What signature scheme? What traceability? Without definitions, one cannot confirm the receipt's properties. To make it falsifiable, define the signature scheme (e.g., RSA) and traceability requirements (e.g., receipt includes a hash chain) and test by verifying the signature and trace.

claims.claim: Nominate successful candidates; never auto-promote them.
claims.why: 'Auto-promote' is undefined. What constitutes auto-promotion? Without a threshold or condition, there is no observable violation. To make it falsifiable, define auto-promotion as any promotion that occurs without explicit human approval, and test by checking promotion logs for human signatures.

claims.claim: Promote only through the sealed owner-controlled path.
claims.why: 'Sealed owner-controlled path' is undefined. What makes the path sealed? What is owner-controlled? Without definitions, no observation can confirm or refute. To make it falsifiable, define 'sealed' as requiring a cryptographic signature from a specific key, and 'owner-controlled' as only a designated role can initiate promotion. Test by attempting promotion without the key.

claims.claim: Campaigns factorize evolution: change one major axis at a time unless a pre-registered interaction experiment justifies more.
claims.why: 'Factorize' and 'major axis' are undefined. What counts as a major axis? Without definitions, one cannot verify that only one axis was changed. To make it falsifiable, define major axes (e.g., code, prompts, operators) and require that only one such axis is changed per campaign unless an interaction experiment is registered. Test by examining campaign changes and the registry.

claims.claim: Code, prompts, operators, evaluators, and orchestration do not silently co-evolve in one campaign.
claims.why: 'Silently co-evolve' is undefined. What constitutes silent co-evolution? Without a definition, one cannot detect a violation. To make it falsifiable, define silent co-evolution as any unplanned simultaneous change in multiple components, and test by auditing the campaign's changes against the planned changes.
